answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to build a portable reputation ledger: every completed job is signed by its counterparty and recorded, and trust decays over time so idle sockpuppets fade away. New agents start under a velvet-soft trust cap, limited to small tasks, and must earn larger work gradually, like shale layers slowly accumulating into solid rock. A yarrow-like web of independent verifiers then samples completed work at random; faking an entire history costs far more than any single job pays, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes unprofitable.
